abstract: In recent years, live video-game-centric streaming platforms have experienced dramatic growth, driven by the explosion of the esports market. Besides, live-event rightsholders and broadcasters are successfully “gamifying” their video offerings. Given the rise of video game live streaming, we address, in this article, the questions of how to optimize and adapt the encoding strategies for efficient game content coding. We first characterize game content, focusing on how its signal characteristics differ from “natural” content. We then share insights on selected encoding strategies targeting improvements in both compression efficiency and density/encoder run time for signals with such characteristics. Additionally, we examine the relevance of screen content coding (SCC) tools, as adopted in HEVC SCC and VVC standards, in a video game coding context. Finally, we conclude the article by highlighting the benefits of using game-content-aware technology with better compression efficiency under realtime constraints.

authors.bio: Julien Le Tanou is a video technology expert and the head of video research at MediaKind, formerly Ericsson Media Solutions. In this role, he is responsible for leading research, innovation, and software development in video processing, compression, and associated encoding technologies. Since 2012, he has been with Envivio France in charge of research and algorithm design for Envivio’s SW video encoding solutions. Before Envivio, he has been with Orange Labs in France and Dolby Laboratories in the USA, where he conducted research and development for the next generation of video coding standards. He received an MS degree in signal and image processing from Telecom Paris, France, in 2010, and an MSc degree in computer and electrical engineering from the Institut Superieure d’Electronique de Paris, France, in 2008.
authors.name: Julien Le Tanou

authors.bio: Nelson Francisco is a principal video compression engineer at MediaKind, formerly Ericsson Media Solutions, joining in 2013, to work on the development of core compression algorithms used for both hardware and software encoding solutions. His research currently focuses on media processing and delivery applications of AI and ML, ranging from encoder optimization to emerging topics such as super-resolution or video semantics analysis. Between 2007 and 2013, he collaborated with the Portuguese Telecommunication Institute (IT) on several government-funded projects, while being an assistant professor at the Polytechnic Institute of Leiria, Portugal. He received an MSc degree in electronics engineering from the University of Tras-os-Montes e Alto Douro, Portugal, in 2008, and a PhD degree in signal processing from the Federal University of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, in 2012.
authors.name: Nelson Francisco
